heard: At 430,000 miles per hour, NASA's fastest craft dives into the sun. Launched in 2018, this mission honors the pioneering astrophysicist Eugene Newman Parker. The project cost approximately $1.5 billion and required extreme engineering to complete the journey. To reach the blistering outer atmosphere, the probe executes seven Venus gravity assists over seven long years. A massive 4.5-inch thick carbon composite heat shield protects the four sensitive instrument suites tucked deep inside. While the exterior withstands temperatures reaching nearly 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit, sensitive internal electronics stay at a constant 85 degrees. That brilliant engineering finally lets humanity directly touch our star at 430,000 miles per hour.
